problem: Find a vector equation of the line that passes through the points $P(-1,5,4)$ and $Q(3,-1,2).$
worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $P$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=p+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $p$ is the position vector of $P.$ 

We can find a direction vector by computing the displacement vector between the given points $P(-1,5,4)$ and $Q(3,-1,2)$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =⟨3,-1,2⟩-⟨-1,5,4⟩ \\  & =⟨4,-6,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector equation of the line is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 5 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -6 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
